result_semantic_payload.summary: The only USDT transfers visible in this device's logs are two entries in /logs/app1.log, both attributed to the logon identity 'chenwei' (30000 USDT on 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT on 2024-03-02 22:43:55, both to destination TBait8888Wallet, each within a couple of minutes of a successful 'chenwei' login from 203.0.113.77 and 198.51.100.23 respectively). This is a log-stated attribution, not an independently authenticated identity: the source scope is a plain text-log export with no Windows artifacts at all (no SAM/SYSTEM registry hives, no Event Log records, no prefetch/amcache), so the log's own user= field is the sole basis for the attribution. The second system's export (/logs/app2.log) contains a same-named 'chenwei' account performing office activity (UPLOAD /shared/annual-plan.docx, PRINT to HQ-3F) from internal 10.20.0.x addresses, but the README states the two systems are unrelated and share no account database. The evidence therefore supports only that two separate systems each recorded an identity string 'chenwei'; it does not support treating them as the same person. There is no cross-system authenticator, no shared token, no common source IP, no corroborating Windows identity evidence, and the IP ranges differ (10.20.0.5/10.20.0.9 internal vs 203.0.113.77/198.51.100.23 external).

claim_candidates.text: The USDT transfers recorded in this device's logs are two entries in /logs/app1.log: 30000 USDT at 2024-03-01 09:15:03 and 12000 USDT at 2024-03-02 22:43:55, both with destination TBait8888Wallet. Both are preceded within ~2 minutes by a successful login attributed to user=chenwei (from 203.0.113.77 and 198.51.100.23 respectively), and the first session ends with a LOGOUT user=chenwei at 09:16:44.

The account identity the logs attribute to the USDT transfers is 'chenwei'. This attribution rests solely on the user= field inside the application log text; no cryptographic, ticket, or OS-level authentication evidence corroborates it.

The second system's log export (/logs/app2.log) also records an account named 'chenwei', performing office activity on 2024-02-20 to 2024-02-22 (LOGIN from 10.20.0.5 and 10.20.0.9, UPLOAD of /shared/annual-plan.docx, PRINT to printer HQ-3F, 12 pages, color=mono).

The two log sources are described as two unrelated internal systems that share no account database, and the README identifies 'chenwei' as a finance-department employee with an office workstation. Because the systems do not share an account database, the identical string 'chenwei' is a coincidence of naming at the level of the evidence, not proof of a shared identity.

Same-named accounts across the two systems CANNOT be treated as the same person on this evidence. There is no shared authenticator, shared account identifier, shared source IP, shared session token, or cross-system join key; the address families differ (10.20.0.x internal vs 203.0.113.77 / 198.51.100.23 external); and the README explicitly states the systems share no account database. It is plausible but unproven that a single individual used the 'chenwei' identity on both systems; the README's note that chenwei is a finance-department employee with an office workstation is consistent with, but does not establish, that the office-workstation activity in app2.log and the externally-sourced USDT transfers in app1.log were performed by the same person.
limitations: No cross-system authentication or identity-binding evidence exists in the captured scope.
README characterization of employees is unverified metadata, not forensic evidence.
External IPs in app1.log (203.0.113.77, 198.51.100.23) are not attributable to any device in the captured scope.
The 'windows' source scope contains no Windows-derived artifacts; all findings derive from three plain-text log/README files.
Account attribution for the USDT transfers rests solely on the user= field in the application log; no authentication evidence (ticket, token, hash, OS logon record) corroborates it.
Log integrity is unverified: no md5 values are recorded for the log files and no signing or hash chain is present.
The README's description of employees and departments is case metadata, not independently verified forensic evidence.
Whether 'chenwei' in app1.log and 'chenwei' in app2.log denote the same person is unresolvable from this scope; the README explicitly states the two systems share no account database.
No on-chain or banking evidence is in scope, so transfer settlement and the identity of the TBait8888Wallet owner are unknown.
warnings: Question premise mismatch: the requested 'windows' scope yielded no Windows evidence; the answer is based on generic text-log files instead.
Identity-trap risk: the same username string appears in both systems; do not merge these into one person without independent identity binding.
IP addresses 203.0.113.77 and 198.51.100.23 belong to the documentation/reserved ranges and are not attributable to any device in the captured scope.
